transcription.tex: For example, \(7\div3=2\text{ remainder }1\), so \(\frac73=2+\frac13\).\par In general, \[\frac{F(x)}{\text{divisor}}=Q(x)+\frac{\text{remainder}}{\text{divisor}},\]where \(Q(x)\) is the quotient.

\textbf{Algebraic division}\par The quotient has degree \(2-1=1\), so it has the form \(Ax+B\).\par \[\begin{array}{r}x^2+5x-9\\-(x^2+2x)\\\hline3x-9\\-(3x+6)\\\hline-15\end{array}\]\par Quotient: \(x+3\). Remainder: \(-15\).
\[\frac{x^2+5x-9}{x+2}=x+3-\frac{15}{x+2}.\]\par \(A=1,\quad B=3,\quad C=-15\).\par \textbf{Tip:} quotient degree equals numerator degree minus divisor degree. Here \(2-1=1\).

transcription.tex: Given that \[\frac{3x^4-2x^3-5x^2-4}{x^2-4}\equiv ax^2+bx+c+\frac{dx+e}{x^2-4},\quad x\ne\pm2,\]find the constants \(a,b,c,d,e\). (4 marks)
Tip: insert \(+0x\) for missing powers before dividing.

\textbf{Alternative: compare coefficients}\par \[\begin{aligned}3x^4-2x^3-5x^2-4&\\&\equiv(ax^2+bx+c)(x^2-4)+dx+e.\end{aligned}\]\par \(a=3,\quad b=-2\).\par \(c-4a=-5\Rightarrow c=7\).\par \(d-4b=0\Rightarrow d=-8\).\par \(e-4c=-4\Rightarrow e=24\).
